newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Advtech jumps on rumours of more purchases.
newsitem.headline: Advtech jumps on rumours of more purchases.

text.p: Shares in Advanced Technical Systems (Advtech), a South African education group, soared to record highs in hectic trade on Thursday on rumours it would announce a number of acquisitions as early as next week.
Dealers said the firm, which has in recent months blazed an acquisition trail through the education and training industry, could add another four buys to its already handsome purchase list.

"There are another four deals in the pipeline...all in the education area. They are looking to buy three more campuses and launching the first Australian MBA degree in South Africa," one equity dealer said.
Advtech management were not available for comment.
Another dealer who said a likely purchase was Boston City Campus, added: "There are rumours floating around and a lot of what looks like insider trading."

Advtech shares on Thursday jumped to a best ever level of 400 cents from a close of 305. The share was the second most active on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) with 1.4 million shares trading in 101 deals.
Shares, which have risen steadily from 26 cents at the beginning of the year, slipped back to end at 315 cents as players took profits, dealers said.
They said a lot of the activity had been jobber-driven, but a single deal of over 900,000 shares showed evidence of institutional interest.

Advtech has this year bought Mast Holdings Ltd, an education and training company, IMD Education Centres, which conducts education courses at tertiary level, and last month snapped up the Global School of Business.
"Advtech has bought all of these at very cheap prices, well below price/earnings," a dealer said.
He predicted earnings for Advtech at 20 cents a share for the year to end February 1997 compared with 7.5 cents in the past year, "even without any new acquisitions".
Advtech is another in a line of private education companies whose shares have shone on the JSE this year amid growing fears about the state of government education.

Included in this group are the Education Investment Corp Ltd which has forecast a doubling in profits to 14.7 million rand in the year to end December 1996. Educor's share closed on Thursday at 310 cents near its best level of 350.
Another example is Leisurenet Ltd which operates sports clubs and recently made a foray into the college sector. Shares on Thursday finished at 360 cents close to a year high of 400.
"Education today is a money-making machine. Parents are prepared to pay enormous amounts for quality private teachers," a trader said.

Events this year have seen South African university and college campuses wrecked by student demonstrations and the Western Cape provincial government threatening to retrench 6,000 teachers amid a funds shortage.
Education Minister Sibusiso Bengu said in May more than 15 million South African adults were illiterate.
